hints: One white piece is attacked and nothing defends it. One white pawn is attacked more often than it is defended. Find both.
The g4 pawn is attacked twice and defended once. Which move gives it a second defender?

items.explain: Rg1 gives the g4 pawn a second defender and leaves the bishop on b5, attacked by the c6 pawn, to its fate. At depth 16 the engine ranks Rg1 first, a little ahead of Ba4 and h4. At depth 22 it rates the position slightly in Black's favour, so Rg1 is a practical gamble. Here a sacrifice is sound only if it is the engine's first choice and rates level or better for the side making it; otherwise it is practical. White has two minor pieces developed (bishop, knight), Black one (knight).

feedback_by_move.b5a4: Saving the bishop is playable, but at depth 16 the engine ranks it below Rg1.
feedback_by_move.h2h4: The pawn attacks the queen, but the bishop on b5 is still attacked; at depth 16 the engine ranks it below Rg1.

feedback_by_move.f3f7: Qxf7+ also leads to mate: at depth 16 the engine finds it within four moves, but Qf6+ mates in two.
